issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Proposition prop:constant estimation (which Prop. prop:projection-regularity restates) bounds sup over the ridge of the third derivative of log p_t by the theta_t-suppressed estimate of Lemma lem:important estimate, whose hypothesis is x in the union of center-dominant regions, and silently replaces the supremum over the ridge by the supremum over the closure of that union. The ridge is not contained in the union of dominant regions: in the paper's own two-point example the ridge is the entire line through the centers, which contains points with split softmax weights (e.g. equal weights at the midpoint, excluded from every B_t^{(i)}(theta_t) for theta_t < 1/2); by Lemma lem:explicit formula the third derivative there is of order a_t^3 R^3/h_t^3 with no theta_t suppression. Hence the proof yields at most the theta-free bound r_t > beta_t h_t^3/(C a_t^3 R^3) ~ h_t^2 R^{-3}; the claimed enhancement r_t > ~ h_t^2 * theta_t^{-1} -> infinity (as theta_t -> 0 arbitrarily subexponentially) is unsupported and contradicts the bounded reach of the bent ridges shown in the paper's own multi-center examples (reach is at most 1/max curvature). Moreover the claimed verification of Assumption assump:ridge set only bounds curvature and asserts 'reach is at least the reciprocal of maximal curvature', presupposing the C^2-manifold/positive-reach property it is supposed to establish. The Stage-1 proof then uses the bogus enhancement: it needs rho_delta = Theta(r_delta) to dominate the noise radius sqrt(h_delta)*||z|| (chi-square threshold d + 2sqrt(d zeta log(1/h)) + 2 zeta log), which the honest theta-free reach (~h^2) cannot provide, so the tube-entry probability is unproven.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove from the data assumption that R_t is a C^2 submanifold with reach of scale ~sqrt(h_t)*polylog (compatible with the chi-square noise radius used in Stage 1), or reformulate Stage 1 with a larger non-projection tube, and restate every rate without the arbitrary theta_t.
issues.overall_effect: The data-dependent verification of the tube/projection framework fails: the stated reach rate is false as quantified, and the Stage-1 entry guarantee (Theorems thm:formal stage 1, thm:informal stage 1), whose Gaussian step needs a tube of radius ~sqrt(h d) while the honest reach is ~h^2, is unsupported; the normal/tangent contraction theorems, whose hypotheses cite only the data assumption, lose the tube machinery their proofs invoke.
issues.title: Reach bound with arbitrary subexponential theta_t is unsupported and false in general
issues.why_classification: No supported resolution avoids new architecture: the theta-enhanced reach must be withdrawn, and rescuing the advertised Stage-1 entry guarantee needs a new geometric argument (reach ~ sqrt(h) near centers) or a redesign of Stage 1, i.e. a comparable version of the reach/entry claims does not survive with the source's tools.

issues.failure_explanation: In both Stage-2 and Stage-3 proofs the drift/forcing estimates are valid only on restricted sets: the ridge expansion of <n, grad log p> uses the ridge definition and Lemma lem:important estimate near the ridge; the center-comparison bound (Lemma lem:application closeness) holds only for x in a center-dominant region; and Pi_t, D_t are defined/C^2 only on the tube. The proofs nevertheless integrate these inequalities over [entry time, T-delta] for the unstopped processes: nothing shows Y_t or tilde Y_t stays in the tube or in a dominant region (the sqrt(2)-diffusion permits excursions, and right after entry the normal drift rate beta_{T-u}-1 is only O(1) while the noise is O(1)). Integrating a conditionally valid inequality along an unstopped path does not yield the stated differential inequality, so the endpoint 'Furthermore' floors of Theorems them:normal contraciton and them:tangent contraciton are not established. (The tangent proof additionally omits the homogeneous Gronwall term exp(-int(1/h-2)) E||tilde u_{t_in}||^2 from its final display, which is only absorbable if constants may depend on R and T.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Work with the stopped distance (stop at the first tube exit, or use the globally defined distance to R_t) and prove an exit-probability/excursion bound, then restate the differential inequalities and endpoint bounds for the stopped processes; the stated rates survive with this contained, standard but nontrivial modification.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative normal-alignment and tangent-sliding bounds of Theorems them:normal contraciton and them:tangent contraciton are not established as stated, and the training-to-inference interface (Theorems thm:inference to training, thm:informal inference to training), which converts these floors into MM^perp/MM^parallel bounds, is unsupported.
issues.title: Normal/tangent contraction proofs integrate regionally valid inequalities without confining the processes
issues.why_classification: A contained localization/stopping argument (plus truncating the endpoint displays) restores the stated rates without new global architecture or loss of the advertised guarantees, but it is more than a routine local patch.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting w = h_t^gamma into the remark's own displayed scalings gives normal-error delta^c * Integral h_t^{1-c-gamma} dt and tangent-error delta^{1/2} * Integral h_t^{1/2-gamma} dt. For gamma = 1 the integrals int_delta^1 h_t^{-c} dt -> 2^{-c}/(1-c) and int h^{-1/2} -> sqrt(2) are O(1) (bulk-dominated), giving O(delta^c) and O(sqrt(delta)) with polynomial-in-T constants, not O(delta); for gamma = 0 one gets O(delta^c (1+T)) and O(sqrt(delta)(1+T)), not O(delta^2). Since c is restricted to [1/2,1), delta^c is never O(delta), and no admissible weight produces the claimed O(delta^2); moreover the claimed strict hierarchy separates w=1 from w=h_t only through constants. The advertised three-tier prediction O(1), O(delta), O(delta^2) -- which the experiments section presents as confirmed -- does not follow from the paper's own bounds.

failure_location.quote: In particular, under weights $w(t)=h_t^2,h_t,1$, the mean-errors along both directions yield $\mc{O}(1),\mc{O}(\delta),\mc{O}(\delta^2)$ respectively, hence inducing different inductive biases in generation.

issues.title: Remark's weight-dependent scalings O(delta), O(delta^2) contradict its own formulas
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained recomputation, but it necessarily withdraws the advertised quantitative regime separation (the delta and delta^2 scalings and the w=1-vs-w=h_t distinction), so it is more than minor and less than a major loss.

issues.failure_explanation: The exact reverse process and the learned-mean process share diffusion coefficient sqrt(2) and differ in drift by 2 h^{-1} e_A. Girsanov's theorem gives KL(path) <= KL(p_T || N(0,I_d)) + (1/4) integral E[ || drift gap ||^2 ] dt = KL(p_T||N) + integral h^{-2} E||e_A||^2 dt = KL_init + eps_A. With Pinsker, the TV term contributing to the probability deficit is sqrt(eps_A/2), not sqrt(eps_A/8): the displayed chain and item (3) of Theorem thm:formal stage 1 claim a KL increment of eps_A/4, which the computation does not yield. The informal Theorem thm:informal stage 1 repeats the same unsupported constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1/8 by 1/2 in the proof display and in Theorems thm:formal stage 1(3) and thm:informal stage 1; a purely local constant correction, no substantive content lost.
issues.overall_effect: The stated high-probability entry bound (items (3) of both stage-1 theorems) is stronger than what the Girsanov step delivers; the qualitative claim (error vanishing with eps_A) survives, but the printed constant is not established.
issues.title: Stage-1 probability bound uses a Girsanov constant four times too small
issues.why_classification: A one-line constant correction preserves every substantive guarantee and rate; the repair is local and forced by the paper's own Girsanov computation.
